feed.title: Sophaxis: changes to the policies
feed.subtitle: Only the changes to the policies, newest first. A change that narrows a right is entered when it is announced, with the day it takes effect.

entry.title: The checked intake: claims are accepted only when public records check them
entry.summary: From 2026-12-01, for a submission whose issue is opened on or after that day, the checked intake accepts a claim only when it can be checked against a source that the claimant does not write at that moment, and turns away the rest. The DOI metadata must list the submitter's ORCID iD; an ORCID record that lists the DOI among its works no longer counts. Every other author confirms in a comment from a GitHub account that their ORCID record links, and must have an ORCID iD in the DOI metadata; a confirmation by email no longer counts. The public ORCID records of every verified author, and of a researcher who vouches, must place them where Sophaxis is offered: no address, current employment or education, and no GitHub location may name a place where it is not offered, the ORCID entries may not name two countries, and one of them must name a place where it is offered and have been added at least 30 days before the issue was opened. To check this, the check reads the countries of public addresses and of current affiliations in ORCID, and the GitHub location, and keeps or writes none of them. A researcher who vouches uses new words: they attest what they know of the submitter, have no conflict of interest and share no current organisation with the submitter in ORCID; this is not a guarantee, and Sophaxis claims no money from them, but an untrue vouching bars them from vouching, is recorded in the history of the record, and the listing is reviewed. A submission that has not passed every check 30 days after its issue was opened is closed, and a new issue can be opened. From the same day, a report of an error in a record is closed if the words it quotes are not on the record page. Removal, withdrawal and personal-data requests, notices of infringement and the withdrawal of a consent are never closed automatically. The Privacy Policy adds the purposes and the items read. Since its publication on 2026-11-14, the submission form no longer asks the submitter to confirm that no author will stay in an excluded place between the submission and the listing; it asks what holds on the day of submission, and, from 2026-12-01, an undertaking to report a change that the submitter learns of before the listing. These changes narrow what authors and researchers who vouch can do, so they are announced on the top page at least 14 days ahead; they apply only to issues opened on or after 2026-12-01. In effect from 2026-12-01. Policies: Submission Policy, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, Moderation Policy.

entry.title: A limit for slight negligence, and what a submitter owes for an untrue confirmation
entry.summary: From 2026-12-01, for a person who agrees to the Terms of Use in a form on or after that day, two clauses apply. For loss that the operator causes in performing the Terms by negligence that is not gross negligence, the operator is liable only for the loss that would ordinarily arise (Article 416(1) of Japan's Civil Code), not for loss arising from special circumstances; the clause says that it applies only to negligence that is not gross negligence, as Article 8(3) of Japan's Consumer Contract Act requires, and it never applies to intent or gross negligence, or to a reader who has not agreed to the Terms. And the submitter undertakes that each confirmation in the form is true when it is made; if a third party makes a claim because one is untrue, the operator tells the submitter and hears them before agreeing to pay anything, and the submitter compensates the operator as Articles 415 and 416 of the Civil Code provide, owing nothing where the untruth is due to a cause for which the submitter is not responsible. Both narrow what an author can claim or add to what an author owes, so they are announced on the top page at least 14 days ahead. They apply only to submissions made on or after that day, and not to earlier agreements. In effect from 2026-12-01. Policies: Terms of Use.

entry.title: What the operator is responsible for, said precisely
entry.summary: The Terms of Use now say that a PDF copy is the deposited file provided as it is and that the work is the deposit in its repository; that nothing on Sophaxis states that a work is correct or of any quality; that the sentence on loss caused only by a work, GitHub, Vercel or a repository speaks of loss to which no intent or negligence of the operator contributed and limits nothing; what the operator is responsible for; that the Takedown Policy is the way to have material removed and takes away no right to go to a court; that no more of a record is kept offline than a review needs; that the Terms take away no claim that the law gives against the operator; and that a clause that excludes or limits the operator's liability applies only as it is written, and is never read as reaching as far as the law allows. Effective on publication, 2026-11-14. Each of these states the Terms as they already stood, or gives authors and readers more; none narrows a right or adds a duty. Policies: Terms of Use.

entry.title: The takedown steps follow Article 3 of Japan's Act on providers
entry.summary: The Takedown Policy now says that, before removing material on a request, the operator shows the authors the material concerned, the right said to be infringed and the reason, and counts the 7 days from the day the question is posted; that a measure goes no further than is needed, and that the parts of a record that a request does not concern are put back once the operator has read it; that for the PDF copies Sophaxis is the sender, so the limitation of Article 3(1) of the Act does not apply to them; and that, for what others write in the issues, the operator follows the conditions of Article 3 of the Act, hiding or editing infringing text without delay once it knows, and otherwise asking the person who wrote it. It also says, in place of an unverified statement that the United States Copyright Office charges a fee, that the limitation of 17 U.S.C. 512(c) needs an agent whose details are given to that Office, and that Sophaxis registers with no office. Effective on publication, 2026-11-14. These give the people concerned more; none narrows a right or adds a duty. Policies: Takedown Policy.

entry.title: The basis of the PDF copies in the Copyright Act
entry.summary: The Copyright Policy now says that keeping and serving a copy are acts that Articles 21 and 23 of Japan's Copyright Act reserve to the copyright holder, that Sophaxis does them only on the permission that the work's licence gives, within its manner and conditions as Article 63 of that Act provides, and relies on no exception of that Act, and that a licence given by someone without the right is not that permission. Effective on publication, 2026-11-14. Nothing that Sophaxis does changes. Policies: Copyright Policy.

entry.title: Advice for the moderator, read by machine, in counts only
entry.summary: Since 2026-11-14, the automatic check gives the moderator advice that decides nothing: whether the licence printed on the first pages of the PDF agrees with the DOI metadata, how many strings shaped like an email address, a telephone number or a postal code appear after the first page outside the authors' own, how many images the PDF embeds, whether the file matches the repository's checksum, and how many affiliations in the DOI metadata, or lines of the first page, name a place where Sophaxis is not offered. The weekly check reads the PDF copies on the site in the same way and compares each with its recorded SHA-256. The comment and the logs show counts and fixed words only. The Moderation Policy and the Privacy Policy, in both languages, say so, and the Privacy Policy names it as a purpose; it keeps nothing, reads no ORCID country, narrows no right and adds no duty. Policies: Moderation Policy, Privacy Policy.

entry.title: A place where offering Sophaxis would not conform to its law is not offered
entry.summary: From 2026-11-29, the Submission Policy says that Sophaxis is also not offered in a place where the operator judges that offering Sophaxis would not conform to the law of that place, and that, when the operator so judges, the place and the reason are added to the table. The rule is also stated in Article 10 of the Statement of Purpose, published on 2026-11-13; that statement creates no rights or obligations, so the rule takes effect through the Submission Policy. This narrows who can be listed, so it is announced on the top page at least 14 days ahead. A place added under it is announced on the top page before it takes effect, as every change to the table is. In effect from 2026-11-29. Policies: Submission Policy.

entry.title: GitHub's notifications can carry a copy of an issue
entry.summary: The Takedown Policy listed what an emptied or deleted issue leaves, and the Privacy Policy said how long the issues stay, without naming GitHub's notifications. GitHub sends a notification of the activity on an issue to the accounts set to receive it, an email notification holds a copy of the content, and the operator's account may be one of them. The Takedown Policy and the Privacy Policy, in both languages, now say that these notifications may carry a copy of the content of an issue, that the copy is handled under GitHub's Terms of Service and Privacy Statement, that the pages of GitHub's documentation that were fetched do not say that it goes away when the issue is emptied or deleted, and that the operator makes no other copy of an issue. This is a correction of an incomplete statement, effective on publication, 2026-11-13. Nothing that Sophaxis does changes; it narrows no right and adds no duty. Policies: Takedown Policy, Privacy Policy.

entry.title: The logs of the automatic steps keep no text of an issue
entry.summary: The Takedown Policy said what an emptied or deleted issue leaves, and did not name the logs of the automatic steps that read it. Until 2026-11-13 those steps received the text of the issue in their environment, which GitHub Actions prints in the log of each run, so the logs kept the text after the issue was emptied. The steps now read the issue from the event file that GitHub Actions gives them, and their logs keep the issue's number and the outcome of each step, not its text. The logs of the runs for the three issues emptied before that day were deleted on 2026-11-13. The Takedown Policy, the Withdrawal Policy and the Privacy Policy, in both languages, now say so, and say that GitHub keeps the logs and the list of runs for the period set for the repository. This is a correction of an incomplete statement, effective on publication, 2026-11-13. It adds a deletion, narrows no right and adds no duty. Policies: Takedown Policy, Withdrawal Policy, Privacy Policy.

entry.title: What the Internet Archive has said about its security
entry.summary: The Privacy Policy said that no statement of the measures the Internet Archive takes to protect personal data was found. The Internet Archive's own copy of its terms page, saved on 2024-01-01, holds a privacy policy dated 10 March 2001 that speaks of standard computer security. The Privacy Policy, in both languages, now quotes it, and still says that the Internet Archive's current terms can be read only with a script running. This is a correction of an untrue statement, effective on publication, 2026-11-13. Nothing that Sophaxis does changes, and no right is narrowed. Policies: Privacy Policy.

entry.title: The address in the OAI-PMH interface is the address for requests
entry.summary: The Privacy Policy said that the OAI-PMH interface gives an email address made for harvesters, and the Takedown Policy said that the address in the OAI-PMH interface is for harvesters, apart from the address for requests. That was untrue: the interface gives the same address as the operator's ORCID record, where requests go. Both policies, in both languages, and the contact page now say so. This is a correction of an untrue statement, effective on publication, 2026-11-13. Nothing that Sophaxis does changes, and no right is narrowed. Policies: Privacy Policy, Takedown Policy.

entry.title: The automatic steps run while GitHub Actions runs
entry.summary: The Takedown Policy and the Terms of Use now say that the automatic steps run as GitHub Actions, that GitHub's terms let it restrict the use of GitHub Actions, and that while Actions does not run the operator takes the steps by hand. A record page reported for exposed personal data is then taken offline by the operator, not at once. The pages promised "at once" without this condition, which Sophaxis could never promise: the step has always run as GitHub Actions. This is a correction of an untrue promise, effective on publication, 2026-11-13. Nothing that Sophaxis does while Actions runs changes, and no right that Sophaxis could give is narrowed. Policies: Takedown Policy, Terms of Use.

entry.title: Dates on the pages are in Japan time
entry.summary: The Terms of Use now say that the dates on Sophaxis's pages, in this feed, in the notices and in the news are dates in Japan time, and that the day a text was fetched is the day in UTC that the record of the fetch keeps. Two entries of this feed, published on 2026-11-13 in Japan time, were dated 2026-11-12, the date by the clock of the work; they are now dated 2026-11-13, and the change to the Copyright Policy took effect on publication, not earlier. The "Last updated" of the pages changed that day is now 2026-11-13. This narrows no right and adds no duty. Policies: Terms of Use.

entry.title: The day from which each place is not offered, in the Privacy Policy
entry.summary: The Privacy Policy said, of the Zenodo community and of the people in the other places that the Submission Policy lists, that the rule applies from 2026-11-22. The Submission Policy gives 2026-11-26 for 15 of the 43 places, as announced. The Privacy Policy now says that the rule applies from the date the Submission Policy gives for each place: 2026-11-22, or 2026-11-26 for 15 of them. Nothing that Sophaxis does changes, and no right is narrowed. Policies: Privacy Policy.

entry.title: PDFs are no longer copied by script from Figshare or Research Square
entry.summary: Effective on publication, 2026-11-13: Sophaxis copies PDFs by script only from Zenodo and arXiv, whose own pages let a script fetch them. Until then, it also copied from Figshare and Research Square, whose terms forbid robots and scripts. The authors of a work at either can attach the deposited PDF to the submission issue instead, as for every other repository. This narrows what authors get. Going on would act against the terms of the two repositories, a legal risk, so the change takes effect on publication, as the Terms of Use allow when a legal risk requires a change sooner, and not earlier. The copies already taken from Figshare stay. Policies: Copyright Policy.

entry.title: In a dispute, the operator aims to answer within 7 days, and a pause holds the answer
entry.summary: From 2026-11-26, the Terms of Use say that, in a dispute, the operator aims to answer within 7 days and does not leave a dispute without reply, and that during a pause described under "Continuity" the answer waits until the pause ends. Until then, the operator answers within 7 days. The words promised an answer in 7 days even while the operator cannot work on Sophaxis at all, which the Terms already allow for; this weakens a promise, so it is announced 14 days ahead. The call for advisers and the policies in brief say the same from the same day. In effect from 2026-11-26. Policies: Terms of Use.

entry.title: Texts by others kept for verification are not under CC BY 4.0
entry.summary: The Licence Policy and the Terms of Use now say that texts by others that the repository quotes, or keeps to verify its quotations, are not licensed under CC BY 4.0 and remain their owners'. They never were the operator's to license. From today the repository keeps whole only laws and other texts that Japan's Copyright Act, Article 13, leaves outside copyright; of every other text it keeps the address, the day, the SHA-256 of the text as fetched, and the parts it quotes or relies on. This narrows no right that anyone held. Policies: Licence Policy, Terms of Use.

entry.title: Fifteen more places where Sophaxis is not offered, and what a person in New Zealand is told
entry.summary: From 2026-11-26, Sophaxis is not offered in 15 more places: Argentina, Colombia, Ghana, Korea, Mexico, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Zimbabwe, Kenya, Tanzania, South Africa, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar. A survey of the laws of 195 countries was made on 2026-11-12, and the data protection laws it found were read at their sources by number. The laws of these places ask for registration, for conditions before personal data leaves the place, for the operator's postal address or telephone number before personal data is collected, or for a parent's consent that the service confirms before the data of a minor is processed; or their data protection law could not be read at its source. The Submission Policy names the law of each. This narrows who can be listed, so it is announced 14 days ahead. From today, the Privacy Policy and the submission form also say that the services outside Japan may not be required to protect personal data with safeguards comparable to those of the law where an author lives, as New Zealand's Privacy Act 2020 asks a person there to be told, and that, for a person in Switzerland, the disclosure to the United States rests on explicit consent; this narrows no right. In effect from 2026-11-26. Policies: Submission Policy, Privacy Policy.

entry.title: The rules on sending users' information outside are met as if they applied
entry.summary: The Privacy Policy now meets the rules of Japan's Telecommunications Business Act on sending users' information outside as if they applied to Sophaxis, and gives, for the one request that a page makes a reader's browser send (the search page's request for the list of records), what is sent, who handles it and for what purpose. The Ministry's Ordinance was fetched and read. None of this narrows a right or adds a duty. Policies: Privacy Policy.

entry.title: The agreement on the court covers only suits based on the Terms
entry.summary: From 2026-11-26, the agreement on the court of first instance, made in a form, covers only suits based on the Terms of Use, or on the submission, listing, correction, withdrawal or removal of the person's own works under them, so that it stays within what Japan's Code of Civil Procedure allows to be agreed. For any other dispute, the court that the law sets has jurisdiction. The agreement stays non-exclusive, and talks and mediation still come first. This may narrow the disputes that can be brought to the agreed court, so it is announced 14 days ahead. In effect from 2026-11-26. Policies: Terms of Use.

entry.title: The mailbox and the request logs, the system of the United States, and the records of provision
entry.summary: The Privacy Policy says that the operator's mailbox at iCloud Mail is provided to users in Japan by iTunes K.K., a company in Japan, which Sophaxis treats as entrusted with it, so that it is not a provision to a third party in a foreign country and no consent is asked of the people who write; that Apple Inc. may handle the emails in the United States; and that Vercel's request logs are not personal information for Sophaxis, with the reasons. It now gives the Personal Information Protection Commission's own information on the system of the United States, what Anthropic says of its measures, and why the measures of OpenAI and xAI cannot be given. It names docs/records-of-provision.md, which gives each recipient's name and address, as part of the record of provision to third parties, kept for at least three years. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty. Policies: Privacy Policy.

entry.title: Why the rules on sending users' information do not apply, Sophaxis as the sender of its records, and the texts fetched again
entry.summary: The Privacy Policy says why the operator considers that the rules of Japan's Telecommunications Business Act on sending users' information outside do not apply: Sophaxis charges for nothing and earns nothing, so it runs no telecommunications business. The Takedown Policy says that, for the record pages and the PDF copies, Sophaxis is itself the sender under Japan's Act on providers of specified telecommunications services, so it does not rely on that Act's limitation of liability, and the operator is liable as Japanese law provides. The texts that the policies quote were fetched again on 2026-11-12, and the Privacy and Submission Policies now quote Article 1 of Russia's Federal Law No. 152-FZ. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty. Policies: Privacy Policy, Takedown Policy, Terms of Use, Submission Policy, Moderation Policy, Copyright Policy.

entry.title: A first sentence for each policy, the steps while the operator cannot work, and numbers in the Japanese translations
entry.summary: Each policy now opens with a sentence that says what it is. The Terms of Use set out, under Continuity, what happens while the operator cannot work at all: who is told, what is paused, what stays online, what still works without the operator, and who could take over. The Japanese translations write durations and dates in Arabic digits, as the English does. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty. Policies: Terms of Use, Submission Policy, Moderation Policy, Copyright Policy, Licence Policy, Privacy Policy, Withdrawal Policy, Takedown Policy.

entry.title: How the criteria for listing change, a feed for policy changes, and no counts of views
entry.summary: The Moderation Policy says how the criteria for listing are reviewed and changed: at least once a year and when a law or a service changes, under the same rules as every other policy, with 14 days' notice for a change that narrows what can be listed. The Terms of Use say that each change to a policy is entered in this feed, which carries nothing else. The Privacy Policy says that no page shows a count of views or downloads, and that Sophaxis keeps no such count. None of these narrows a right or adds a duty. Policies: Moderation Policy, Terms of Use, Privacy Policy.

entry.title: Changes announced on the top page, before this feed began
entry.summary: Changes to these policies were announced on the top page before this feed began. They take effect in steps, from 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-25, as the notice on the top page and each policy say. In effect from 2026-11-21. Policies: Terms of Use, Submission Policy, Moderation Policy, Licence Policy, Privacy Policy, Takedown Policy.

entry.title: The feed begins
entry.summary: Each of the eight policies was last changed on 2026-11-11. Earlier versions, and every change to them, are kept in the history of the public repository. From this day, each change to a policy is also entered here. Policies: Terms of Use, Submission Policy, Moderation Policy, Copyright Policy, Licence Policy, Privacy Policy, Withdrawal Policy, Takedown Policy.
